answers.value: P - iv; Q - i; R - ii; S - iii
answers.working:
Work through each description.

**P.** A notochord and a dorsal hollow nerve cord are the defining features of the phylum **Chordata** (iv).

**Q.** Cyclostomes (lampreys, hagfish) are ectoparasites on fishes, have 6 to 15 pairs of gill slits and a closed circulatory system, so Q matches **Cyclostomata** (i).

**R.** Cartilaginous fishes (sharks, rays) are marine, keep their notochord throughout life and have tiny placoid scales, so R matches **Chondrichthyes** (ii).

**S.** Hemichordates such as Balanoglossus have an open circulatory system and a stomochord (a notochord-like structure in the collar), so S matches **Hemichordata** (iii).

The set P - iv, Q - i, R - ii, S - iii is option (A). So the answer is option (A).

Chromosomes are named by where the **centromere** (primary constriction) lies along them. A metacentric chromosome has the centromere in the middle, giving two equal arms; sub-metacentric has it slightly away from the middle; acrocentric has it close to one end; telocentric has it at the very end.

Telomeres are the chromosome tips, and the centriole and centrosome are not parts of a chromosome at all. So the answer is option (A).

answers.value: Three fatty acid chains linked to a molecule of glycerol
answers.working:
A **triglyceride** (a fat or oil) forms when each of the three hydroxyl groups of one glycerol molecule is esterified with a fatty acid. So it is one glycerol carrying three fatty acid chains.

Option (B) reverses the numbers, option (C) describes nothing real, and cholesterol (option D) is a sterol, not part of a triglyceride. So the answer is option (A).

answers.value: It is an accessory pigment which absorbs light at 600 - 700 nm.
answers.working:
Check each statement about carotenoids.

(A) True: carotenoids protect chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation by quenching excess energy.

(B) True: in ripening fruits such as tomato, chloroplasts turn into chromoplasts that store carotenoids.

(C) True: abscisic acid, the plant stress hormone, is made from a carotenoid precursor.

(D) False: carotenoids are accessory pigments, but they absorb in the **blue region (about 400 to 500 nm)**, which is why they look yellow or orange. The 600 to 700 nm red region is absorbed mainly by chlorophylls.

So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: D
answers.working:
In the electron transport chain, electrons from NADH enter at **Complex I** and electrons from \(\mathrm{FADH_2}\) enter at **Complex II**. Both routes pass electrons to ubiquinone, then to Complex III, cytochrome c, Complex IV and oxygen.

**Experiment 1 (chemical X):** the step Complex I to ubiquinone is blocked, so NADH cannot feed the chain. But electrons from \(\mathrm{FADH_2}\) still enter at ubiquinone through Complex II and pass on to oxygen, so some ATP is still made.

**Experiment 2 (chemical Y):** the step Complex III to cytochrome c is blocked. Every electron, from NADH and from \(\mathrm{FADH_2}\), must pass this step, so electron flow and oxidative ATP synthesis stop almost completely.

**Experiment 3 (untreated):** the full chain works and ATP synthesis is highest.

So ATP made is Experiment 2 \(<\) Experiment 1 \(<\) Experiment 3, which is option (D).

answers.label: A
answers.value: Levels of renin, angiotensin I and II and aldosterone are increased.
answers.working:
A fall in glomerular filtration rate is sensed by the **juxtaglomerular apparatus**, whose JG cells release **renin**.

Renin converts angiotensinogen into **angiotensin I**, which is converted into **angiotensin II**. Angiotensin II constricts blood vessels, raising glomerular blood pressure and so GFR, and it also stimulates the adrenal cortex to release **aldosterone**, which increases reabsorption of \(\mathrm{Na^+}\) and water.

So all four (renin, angiotensin I, angiotensin II and aldosterone) rise. So the answer is option (A).

answers.label: C
answers.working:
Oxygen leaves oxyhaemoglobin most readily under the conditions found in active tissues: low \(\mathrm{pO_2}\), high \(\mathrm{pCO_2}\), **high \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration (low pH)** and **higher temperature**. These shift the oxygen dissociation curve to the right (the Bohr effect), so haemoglobin gives up more oxygen.

Lower \(\mathrm{[H^+]}\) and lower temperature, as in the alveoli, favour oxygen binding instead. So the answer is option (C).

answers.value: Red muscle fibres produce ATP aerobically under normal oxygen conditions.
answers.working:
**Red muscle fibres** are rich in myoglobin and contain many mitochondria, so they make ATP mainly by aerobic respiration. **White muscle fibres** have little myoglobin and few mitochondria, and rely more on anaerobic glycolysis.

(A) is false: red fibres have more mitochondria. (B) is false: red fibres are mainly aerobic. (C) is false: lactic acid builds up more in white fibres, which depend on anaerobic respiration. (D) is correct. So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: D
answers.working:
In flowering plants, meiosis happens before gamete formation: the megaspore mother cell divides by meiosis to give a **haploid megaspore**. This megaspore then divides by **mitosis** (three rounds) to form the 8-nucleate embryo sac, one of whose cells is the egg. So in garden pea the female gamete comes from mitosis of haploid cells.

In fruit fly and chicken, eggs are formed directly by meiosis of diploid cells. In the honey bee, it is the haploid **male** that makes gametes by mitosis; the queen (diploid female) makes eggs by meiosis. So the answer is option (D).

The anticodon pairs with the codon in an **antiparallel** way, A with U and G with C.

Anticodon 5'-G U U-3' pairs with 3'-C A A-5' on the mRNA. Read in the usual 5' to 3' direction, the codon is 5'-AAC-3'.

AAC codes for **asparagine**, so this tRNA carries asparagine. Option (C), CAA, is the trap you get by pairing without reversing the direction. So the answer is option (B).

answers.value: R1 = ppQQ ; R2 = PPqq ; R3 = PPQQ ; R4 = ppqq
answers.working:
With linked genes, the **parental (non-recombinant) gametes** are the most frequent and the recombinant gametes are the least frequent.

**First cross:** the frequent gametes are pQ and Pq (35% each), so the F1 received the chromosome pQ from one parent and Pq from the other. True-breeding parents that give these are **ppQQ** and **PPqq**. So R1 = ppQQ and R2 = PPqq (PQ and pq, 15% each, are recombinants).

**Second cross:** the frequent gametes are PQ and pq (35% each), so the parents were **PPQQ** and **ppqq**. So R3 = PPQQ and R4 = ppqq.

Only option (D) gives both pairs correctly. Option (A) has the first cross right but the second cross swapped. So the answer is option (D).

answers.value: A group of viruses with RNA genome and reverse transcriptase activity
answers.working:
**Retroviruses** (such as HIV) carry RNA as their genetic material. After infecting a cell, they use the enzyme **reverse transcriptase** to copy their RNA into DNA, which then joins the host genome. The name comes from this reverse flow of information, RNA to DNA.

So the answer is option (B).

answers.label: B
answers.value: Circular plasmid pIAT25 with X sites at 9235 bp and 4235 bp, and Y sites at 1235 bp and 6235 bp
answers.working:
Read the gel lane by lane for a circular plasmid of 10,000 bp.

**Lane X:** one band at 5 kb. Cutting a circle at two sites gives two pieces, and they run as one band only if both are 5 kb. So the two X sites are 5000 bp apart.

**Lane Y:** likewise, the two Y sites are 5000 bp apart.

**Lane X + Y:** bands at 3 kb and 2 kb, so the four sites alternate and the gaps are 3000 and 2000 bp.

Now test the maps.

- (A) X at 9235 and 6235 are 3000 bp apart, not 5000. Wrong.
- (C) Y at 9235 and 6235 are 3000 bp apart. Wrong.
- (D) X at 9235 and 1235 are 2000 bp apart. Wrong.
- (B) X at 4235 and 9235 are 5000 bp apart; Y at 1235 and 6235 are 5000 bp apart. In order the sites are 1235 (Y), 4235 (X), 6235 (Y), 9235 (X), giving fragments of 3000, 2000, 3000 and 2000 bp (the last one wraps from 9235 back to 1235). These run as the 3 kb and 2 kb bands.

So the answer is option (B).

answers.label: B
answers.value: Honey bee males cannot have daughters but can have sons.
answers.working:
In honey bees, males (drones) develop from **unfertilised** eggs and are haploid, while females develop from **fertilised** eggs and are diploid (statement A is correct).

A drone's sperm can only fertilise an egg, and a fertilised egg always becomes a female. So a male can have **daughters but never sons**. Statement (B) says the opposite, so it is incorrect.

Being haploid, a drone makes sperm by mitosis, while the diploid queen makes eggs by meiosis (C is correct). A drone has no father, but his mother came from a fertilised egg, so he does have a grandfather (D is correct).

So the answer is option (B).

answers.label: B
answers.value: More than 80% of the solar energy incident on earth is captured by plants and photosynthetic bacteria.
answers.working:
Plants capture only a tiny share of the sunlight that reaches the earth. Less than 50% of incident radiation is photosynthetically active (PAR), and plants and photosynthetic bacteria fix only about **2 to 10% of the PAR**. So the claim of more than 80% is false.

The other statements are correct: energy flows one way, from producers to higher trophic levels (A); to estimate the energy of a trophic level, all organisms at that level must be counted (C); and by the **10% law**, only about 10% of energy passes to each next trophic level (D).

So the answer is option (B).
